I will keep my planting simple and steady this year. In Quzhou County, the land, weather, and water conditions fit the usual winter wheat and summer maize rotation best, and at my age I would rather grow crops I know well than take risks on something harder to manage. I will put all my land into this rotation, because it spreads work across the year, the buyers are easy to find, and I understand the field operations clearly. For wheat, I will use an improved variety, apply moderate fertilizer, irrigate a few key times, and keep weed and disease control to a small number of sprays. After wheat harvest, I will plant hybrid summer maize right away to catch the season, give it enough nitrogen, and manage water and pests in a simple way. I will use rotary tillage because it is easier for me to handle than deep ploughing every time, and it keeps the work practical.
